What is a Scottsdale chauffeur and black car service?

A professionally driven car booked by the hour or as a transfer, not a rideshare with a nicer badge. Black-car vehicles carry it here, from the 6-seat Luxury SUV (Suburban) at $125 an hour to the Maybach Jet Sprinter at $295 an hour, each on a 4-hour minimum when you book time. Two shapes cover it. A transfer is one price between two addresses, no minimum — an arrival or a dinner drop — flat within 15 road miles from pickup to drop-off, and priced from the drive beyond that, with the empty return included. An hourly booking buys the vehicle and chauffeur for a block of time; inside it the car follows your schedule. The difference is the clock, not the car: the same Executive Black Sprinter runs an airport transfer at $295 and an as-directed evening at $145 an hour. Who is driving never changes: "A professional chauffeur on every vehicle, background- and MVR-checked"

All chauffeured, all on published rates: the Luxury SUV (Suburban) at $125 an hour, both 14-seat executive Sprinters at $145 an hour, the Maybach Shuttle Sprinter at $195 an hour and the Maybach Jet Sprinter at $295 an hour. An hourly booking opens at $500. Read the table as a rate card, not a ranking. How does a black car transfer from Phoenix Sky Harbor work?

As a trip with no hourly minimum: $225 one way in the Luxury SUV (Suburban), $295 in an executive Sprinter, $550 in the Maybach Jet Sprinter. Give us the flight number and the flight is tracked. Each added stop costs $50. The desk publishes the pricing rule in full: "Airport and point-to-point transfers are priced as a trip with no hourly minimum — flat within 15 road miles from pickup to drop-off, and longer transfers priced from the drive with the empty return included. An hourly charter starts at four hours on every vehicle except the 56-passenger motorcoach, which starts at five. Each extra stop on a transfer is $50, and stops on an hourly charter cost nothing. Anything the online quote cannot price — an unusual route, a multi-vehicle movement, a vehicle we hold for request only — goes to the reservations desk and comes back as a written quote before any card is charged." So an arrival is usually the cheaper booking — one trip rather than 4 hours — while a day that starts at the airport and runs on through meetings is buying hours, and the transfer price stops being the right comparison. We print no curb, gate or drive time; none are ours to set. What is ours: "Flight tracking on airport legs" — and "Count bags, not just seats. Say up front if the group is carrying golf travel bags, ski bags or boxed gear, because those decide the vehicle more often than the headcount does." The airport Sprinter page and the Phoenix airport to Scottsdale guide carry the rest.

How does an hourly as-directed chauffeur work for dinners, golf and corporate days?

You book a block of hours and the car is yours inside it. The minimum is 4 hours on every vehicle on this page, so an as-directed evening starts at $500 in the Luxury SUV (Suburban) or $580 in an executive Sprinter, and stops inside the block cost nothing extra. Dinner in Old Town Scottsdale with a stop before and a ride home after is one booking, not three; a golf day out to North Scottsdale is one booking with a long wait in the middle. "Ask your chauffeur for anything. Stops, temperature, volume, a photo. Really." The executive Sprinter's own operational note is the practical half: "Put a street address on the reservation rather than a landmark, and give us the mobile number of whoever is actually meeting the vehicle. Your chauffeur photographs the interior before every trip for our records, so tell them straight away if anything is wrong when you board." Corporate days scale without becoming a different product: on request the desk writes "A written movement plan before the date — vehicle by vehicle, pickup by pickup". A programme that outgrows one cabin is a shuttle question.

Which private events does a chauffeur service cover?

Anything with a fixed arrival and a loose ending: galas, fundraisers, art walks, a wedding as a guest, a milestone dinner, a concert, an anniversary. Every vehicle here does private-event work on the same rate card, and the 4-hour minimum usually covers the evening already. An hourly booking pays for itself twice here: nobody parks, and the return is arranged before the evening runs late. The vehicle waits out of the way and the same chauffeur takes the group home. Fit is the only real decision — 6 in the Luxury SUV (Suburban), 14 in either executive Sprinter, or Up to 28 across 2 Executive Black Sprinters when one cabin is not enough. The house rule that matters most on an event night: "No eating or food inside the vehicle. Drinks are fine; snacks wait for the next stop." And what we will not promise early: "Availability on your date, which is confirmed in writing before anything is reserved."

How do the deposit and cancellation work?
